title: Elderflower drizzle cake
subtitle: a light lemon sponge soaked with an elderflower and lemon syrup
excerpt: Elderflower drizzle cake is a lemon drizzle variant where the syrup uses elderflower cordial alongside lemon juice to give it a fragrant, floral quality. The syrup is spooned over the cake as soon as it comes out of the oven so it soaks in while the crumb is still hot and open. The result is a moist, fragrant loaf with a sugary crust.
sourceNotes: Elderflower drizzle cake, a British lemon drizzle variant with elderflower cordial, widely published in British home-baking books from the 2000s onward.

glossaryTerms.definition: A sugar syrup poured over a freshly baked sponge to permeate the crumb while the cake is still hot. The sugar crystallises slightly at the surface as it cools, forming a thin, crunchy crust.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the un-drizzled cake, wrapped tightly in cling film. Defrost at room temperature and drizzle after thawing.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The soaked cake improves overnight as the syrup distributes. Keeps for up to 4 days in an airtight tin.

content.text: The sponge is a standard all-in-one method: all the ingredients go into the bowl at once. The lemon zest goes into the batter and the elderflower and lemon juice go into the
, which is spooned over the moment the loaf comes out of the oven. The cake is done when a skewer comes out clean and the sponge feels just set to the touch.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan. Grease a 900 g loaf tin and line with baking parchment.
Put the butter, caster sugar, eggs, flour, and lemon zest into a large bowl. Beat with a hand mixer or stand mixer on medium speed for 2 minutes until pale and well combined.
Spoon into the prepared tin and bake for 45 to 50 minutes until golden on top, springy to the touch, and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
While the cake is baking, mix together the elderflower cordial, lemon juice, and granulated sugar in a small bowl. The sugar will not fully dissolve at this stage.

As soon as the cake comes out of the oven, prick the top all over with a skewer. Spoon the elderflower-lemon soak slowly over the surface, pausing to let it absorb. The granulated sugar will form a light crust as it dries.
Leave to cool in the tin for 30 minutes, then carefully remove and cool completely on a wire rack.

attrs.problem: Soak pooling on the surface and not absorbing
attrs.avoid: Avoid pouring all the soak at once; the cake needs time to absorb between spoonfuls.
attrs.fix: Add the soak a tablespoon at a time, letting each addition absorb for about 30 seconds before adding more.

attrs.problem: Cake dense and did not rise evenly
attrs.avoid: Avoid opening the oven before 35 minutes, as the sponge will sink.
attrs.fix: Check the oven temperature with a thermometer; fan oven temperatures can vary by 10 to 15 degrees.
